notes_list.title: Aromatic One-Liners
notes_list.basic_overview: Friedel–Crafts alkylation → aryl alkyl; Friedel–Crafts acylation → aryl ketone; Reimer–Tiemann → ortho-hydroxybenzaldehyde from phenol; Kolbe–Schmitt → salicylic acid framework; Gattermann–Koch → aromatic aldehyde.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
Use substrate clues: phenol + CHCl3/base → Reimer–Tiemann; sodium phenoxide + CO2 → Kolbe–Schmitt; benzene + RCOCl/AlCl3 → Friedel–Crafts acylation.

MECHANISM & STEPWISE EXPLANATION
The source describes the transformation as: Friedel–Crafts alkylation → aryl alkyl; Friedel–Crafts acylation → aryl ketone; Reimer–Tiemann → ortho-hydroxybenzaldehyde from phenol; Kolbe–Schmitt → salicylic acid framework; Gattermann–Koch → aromatic aldehyde. The mechanism should be read as activation of the stated substrate, formation of the key reactive intermediate, the bond-making/bond-breaking event described by the reaction, and the stated work-up/product-forming step.

1. Activate the stated substrate with the listed reagent/conditions.
2. Generate the key reactive intermediate or electrophile/nucleophile implied by the reaction.
3. Carry out the characteristic bond-forming, bond-breaking or rearrangement step.
4. Complete proton transfer/work-up and verify the characteristic product.
